title: Sister-in-law's wedding on our honeymoon
author: Storytime
hook: My sister-in-law scheduled her wedding during our honeymoon. Then we found out where.
story: My husband Jake and I got married in October. We'd saved for two years for our honeymoon. Ten days in Bali. His sister, Brianna, knew our dates. Everyone did. A month before our wedding, Brianna announced her own wedding date. The same week as our honeymoon. She said, it was the only date the venue had. And Jake, you're my best man, so you'll have to come back early. Jake said no. Brianna cried to their mom. Their mom called us selfish. We went to Bali anyway. On day three, we walked into the hotel lobby, and there was a giant sign. Welcome to the wedding of Brianna and Tyler. Same hotel. Same week. Her fiancé, Tyler, is a travel agent. He'd seen our booking on the family group chat and moved their whole wedding there. Brianna said, see, now you don't have to miss it! Forty guests. In our honeymoon hotel. Jake's mom hugged us like nothing happened. And Brianna had already put Jake's name on the best man seating card. The wedding is in two days. Do we go?
caption: she moved her wedding to our honeymoon 🌴 #storytime

title: My brother proposed during my wedding toast
author: Storytime
hook: My brother proposed to his girlfriend during my wedding toast. I took the microphone back. Then she told me something.
story: My wedding was last month. My little brother Danny gave a toast. It was sweet, funny, perfect. Then he said, and since everyone I love is here, and turned around. He got down on one knee in front of his girlfriend, Mia. Two hundred guests gasped. Mia looked at me. Frozen. I didn't think. I walked over, took the microphone, and said, Danny, not today. Some people clapped. Most went silent. Danny was humiliated. Mia ran outside. My mom called me heartless. An hour later, I found Mia crying in the parking lot. I apologized. She shook her head and said, no. Thank you. She said she'd told Danny, twice, that she never wanted a public proposal. That she'd been planning to propose to him herself. At Christmas. At the lake where they met. She had the ring in her purse. She showed me. Danny never listened. Now Danny won't speak to me, and Mia asked me not to tell him why. My whole family thinks I ruined his moment. Should I tell them the truth?
caption: I took the mic back for a reason 🎤 #storytime

title: My aunt mocked my cheap Thanksgiving
author: Storytime
hook: This year I hosted Thanksgiving on a tight budget. My rich aunt laughed at it. Then she asked for seconds.
story: Money's been tight for me this year. When my family asked me to host Thanksgiving, I said yes, but I had a budget of eighty dollars for fourteen people. I got creative. Dollar store gravy. Boxed stuffing with fresh herbs. A turkey breast instead of a whole bird. My aunt Diane walked in, looked at the table, and said loudly, oh, it's a budget Thanksgiving. How fun. She drives a Mercedes. She brought nothing. All night, she made comments. Is this the store brand? I didn't know they made gravy in a packet. Then she went back for seconds. And thirds. She asked for the stuffing recipe. Twice. Later, while everyone was watching football, I found her in the kitchen, quietly packing leftovers into containers. A lot of leftovers. She looked up, and her eyes were wet. She said, please don't tell anyone. We lost everything this year. The house is in foreclosure. The Mercedes is leased. She hasn't told her own kids. She asked if she could take some food home. I gave her all of it. Should I tell the family, or keep her secret?
caption: the rich aunt took the leftovers home 🦃 #storytime
sound: a warm acoustic guitar with a bittersweet turn at very low volume
why: Budget Thanksgiving dinners are trending, the rich aunt's mocking makes viewers angry, the foreclosure twist flips sympathy, and keep her secret pulls emotional comments.
